title: Navitas and Microchip collaborate on 800V reference design for AI data centers
source_used: Semiconductor Today (its report on the joint Navitas and Microchip announcement)
key_facts: Navitas Semiconductor (Torrance, California) and Microchip Technology (Chandler, Arizona) have collaborated on an 800V DC-to-6V DC reference design for AI data-centre rack power; announced 5 Oct 2026.

The industry is shifting toward 800V DC rack power architectures to improve distribution efficiency and power density for high-power GPU clusters; the design is aligned with the Open Compute Project (OCP) 800V DC standard.
It combines Microchip's digital power control and security parts (dsPIC33AK digital signal controllers, TA100 CryptoAuthentication device) with Navitas's GaNFast gallium nitride (GaN) power devices.
The power board uses 16 GaN transistors and targets up to 96% peak efficiency at full load, with a power density of 2,100 watts per cubic inch, and is about 20% thinner than a mobile phone.
It converts 800V DC straight to 6V DC, combining the 800V-to-50V and 50V-to-6V stages in one converter.
It will come with a reference board, software and documentation, and is being showcased at Microchip's event at the 2026 OCP Global Summit in San Jose, California (12 to 15 Oct).
Quotes come from Microchip's Joe Thomsen and Navitas's Vipin Bothra; the efficiency and density figures are stated targets from the companies.
Semiconductor Today's page is a report built on the companies' announcement; the wire press release (GlobeNewswire, 5 Oct 2026) is blocked here.
quote_evidence: To help accelerate this transition, power semiconductor firm Navitas Semiconductor Corp of Torrance, CA, USA and Microchip Technology Inc of Chandler, AZ, USA have collaborated on an 800V DC-to-6V DC reference design for AI data-center rack power applications.
The PDB targets delivering up to 96% peak efficiency at full load with 1MHz switching frequency, enabling a power density of 2100W/in3.
The solution is being showcased at Microchip’s event at the 2026 Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit in San Jose, CA, USA (12–15 October).
why_it_matters_hint: Higher-voltage rack power is meant to make AI data-centre power distribution more efficient, and a ready-made design shortens the work for builders.
notes: Pool item is Semiconductor Today's report of a joint Navitas and Microchip press release (GlobeNewswire, 5 Oct 2026, wire page not reachable here); credited to Semiconductor Today. Company claims and targets, not independently tested; no customer or launch date named.
